subject: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: validate model fit for Aurelia’s summarization + clinical triage flows (short clinical notes -> disposition/action) with a small, customer-specific eval before committing to a rollout.
- Redwood will run a controlled evaluation against your sample dataset and the prompt sets you shared. We’ll produce token-cost, latency, and quality metrics (automated + sampled human review).

Ask from your side: please upload the redacted sample dataset (CSV) and the prompt set you prefer to the Drive folder we discussed. If there is any PII remaining, mark it explicitly so we can enable redaction/PII-scrubbing during the eval run.

Attached: aurelia_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt templates), aurelia_sample_dataset_redacted.csv (example row-level format). Also attaching our internal runbook (redwood-eval-runbook.pdf) — it shows the dataset format we prefer and the scoring rubric.

Proposed high-level eval plan & timeline: 
- Day 0 (this week): we get the redacted dataset + confirm scoring rubric (you/or Priya).
- Day 1–2: Redwood ingest + sanity checks (data format, label coverage).
- Day 3: trial runs across 3 candidate models (see recommended models below), automated scoring and quick sampling for human spot-check.
- Day 4: delivery of report & scoring dashboard, joint review call to decide next steps.

Recommended candidate models (balance accuracy vs unit cost):
1) meta-llama-2-70b-chat (quantized q4f16) — best for complex instruction-following across long context.
2) redwood-13b-instruct (8-bit) — cost-efficient, good for structured summarization prompts.
3) mosaicml-instruct-34b (int8) — middle ground for throughput/quality.

Scoring we plan to run (automated): exact-match for structured labels, ROUGE-L for summarization, embedding-similarity (cosine on instruction-tuned embeddings) with threshold bands, and a small human-labeled sample (5-10% of cases) to compute precision/recall for key entities.

Open items for you: confirm the evaluation success criteria (example: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 on summaries OR human accept rate >= 85% for clinical action suggestions), and any constraints around storing the dataset in our private environment.

Next steps: once you confirm the dataset upload + success metric, I’ll schedule the eval run and assign Neha as the technical lead for the job. Karthik will own commercial/contract questions.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick sync if you want to walk through the dataset together.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: aurelia_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 2KB), aurelia_sample_dataset_redacted.csv (CSV, 120KB), redwood-eval-runbook.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear plan. We’ll do the following: 

- Priya will upload the redacted CSV and the prompt set to the Drive folder by end of day Monday (we’re finishing a quick sanity pass).
- One constraint: a portion of our dataset contains PHI related to free-text clinician notes. We can provide a redacted derivative but want confirmation on the following before upload: where will the data be stored for the evaluation (Redwood hosted vs dedicated private), and will it be encrypted at rest with our KMS?

On scoring: the ROUGE-L threshold you proposed sounds reasonable as a starting point, but our clinical QA team also wants the embedding-similarity approach you mentioned — they prefer a percentile-based threshold (top 10% similarity flagged as pass) combined with human review on borderline cases.

Also, timeline-wise, can you confirm the expected turnaround once we upload? We have a stakeholder demo planned week of Feb 23 and would like the initial report before then if possible.

Alex
Head of Product, Aurelia Health
alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com

---
Forwarded attachment: link to Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAureliaEval

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health

Internal — forwarding Alex’s reply and the Drive link. Quick tech asks and proposed defaults for the eval job: 

Tech asks (Neha):
- Can we run the eval in their dedicated Private environment, or are they ok with Redwood-hosted ephemeral storage with customer KMS? Alex has asked specifically about KMS/encryption at rest.
- Data format validation: the sample has a CSV with these columns: id, clinician_note, structured_inputs (json string), expected_action (label), expected_summary. Confirm we can parse structured_inputs and normalized labels.

Proposed Redwood defaults for the run (so we can communicate back):
- Ingest: CSV via Drive link -> S3 staging (encrypted) -> optional automatic PII-redaction pass.
- Eval job config: pin models: [meta-llama-2-70b-chat@v1.2-q4f16, redwood-13b-instruct@v2.0-8bit, mosaicml-instruct-34b@v1.1-int8]; temperature 0.0 for deterministic outputs, max_tokens 256, batch_size 32, streaming off for eval runs.
- Scoring pipeline: exact-match for expected_action, ROUGE-L for expected_summary, embedding-similarity using redwood-embed-3 small model (cosine), and human sampling 7% with a randomized stratified sample across labels.
- Failure modes: if more than 15% of rows are malformed or missing expected_label, we’ll pause and send a data-cleaning checklist to Priya.

Commercial/ops notes (Karthik / Monica):
- If they require the eval to run inside a Private VPC with their KMS, that will likely move this to a paid Private engagement (we should flag to AE/Commercial team). Karthik, please advise on minimum commitment and ETS.

Neha — can you confirm the ingestion/PII-scrub steps and whether the automatic redaction can remove PHI reliably for clinician notes? If not, we’ll ask Aurelia to provide a synthetically redacted derivative.

Thanks — I’ll update Alex once we have these confirmations.

Rachel

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health

Thanks team — quick answers: 

- We uploaded the redacted CSV and the prompt set to the Drive folder this morning (file names match Rachel’s attachments). Link in Alex’s message.
- We cannot run the data in a non-customer-controlled KMS for the full dataset. For evaluation purposes, we can either: (A) provide a synthetically redacted derivative (no PHI) that can be processed in Redwood-hosted evals, or (B) allow a one-time ingest into our Private VPC with our KMS (requires procurement steps).
- Timeline: we need the report by Feb 20 to prep for the stakeholder meeting Feb 23 — is that feasible?

We’ll wait on Neha’s note about whether automatic redaction meets clinical QA standards.

Priya Shah
Senior Product Ops, Aurelia Health
priya.shah@aureliahealth.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aureliahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model eval playbook & data handoff — Aurelia Health

Great — thanks for the upload and clarity on the KMS requirements. Short answers and next steps: 

- Option A (preferred for speed): we’ll run the eval on the synthetically redacted derivative in Redwood-hosted eval infra. This gets us the fastest turnaround (target report by Feb 20). Please confirm which file in the Drive is "synthetic_redacted" vs the partial PHI sample.
- Option B (if they need the exact-source data): we can run inside a Private VPC with their KMS, but this will require a short procurement/ops window — Karthik, can you provide a rough lead time and estimate?

Neha — please do the following once Priya confirms which file to use:
1) Ingest the CSV from Drive link -> run the PII auditor (report expected in ~2 hours).
2) Apply our standard cleaning: normalize JSON in structured_inputs, validate label enums, drop rows with missing expected_action (report the count).
3) Kick off the three-model eval with the pinned versions I listed; set sampling for human review to 7%; create the eval dashboard link and share with Alex + Priya.

Karthik — please flag any procurement hurdles or minimum Private engagement terms to me this afternoon; if Option B is required we’ll pause the schedule and coordinate with Aurelia’s procurement. 

Alex / Priya — once Neha confirms the ingestion pass is green I’ll schedule the short review call for Feb 20 (30 minutes) and we’ll distribute the dashboard ahead of the call.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
